this is the only lens whose source carries no severity calibration at all; the whole section is authored. Three gates in order (anchored, not a single endpoint, not another lens control), a tier cap, a twelve-row severity table and two rules that override the table

the anchor rule is a hard gate rather than a downgrade mechanism: every threat cites a specific file with a line, a specific configuration key and its value, or an explicitly stated architectural assumption. An un-anchored threat is not a finding - it moves to Assumptions to confirm with no severity, no candidate_id and no line in the findings table

Gate 2: a threat resolving to one endpoint, handler, function or file is not a threat-model finding at all and is handed to the lens that owns the unit, usually web-and-api with the file and line. A threat-model finding is about a relationship - two or more components, a crossing, a shared resource, or a path

every severity row names the artifact that establishes its condition, and the preamble states that if the named artifact cannot be found the row does not apply and the threat goes to Assumptions to confirm - so no condition can silently downgrade a finding forever. The Critical composite-pivot row requires three artifacts (an exposure artifact, a credential artifact reachable at hop 1, a data artifact) and drops to High if any hop rests on an assumption

the project tier table caps T0 static reasoning at Medium, so the severity column is read as claimed_impact_severity and effective_severity reaches High or Critical only when a T1 proof lands or triage elevates on another lens proven finding
severity_floor is presentational: it orders this lens findings and never suppresses one
